Subject: Renewal question — phased upsize + go-live cutover

Hi Michael,

Quick background: our current Redwood contract ends 2026-12-31. We expect a meaningful product launch in Q2'27 that will double inference traffic, so we're looking to commit earlier and smooth billing across FY27. Procurement asked whether we can: (1) move to a 2-year term that co-terms to calendar years, (2) front-load a portion of credits to cover Q1 ramp, and (3) carve a cutover window where we can burst above committed capacity while the new infra is validated.

Can you sketch how Redwood would structure a renewal to: multi-year, include a graduated ramp schedule, include an auto-renew opt-out by finance, and an explicit surge/cutover safety band? Also, any doc templates (SOW, checklists) you normally share would help.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if easier.

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask. TL;DR: we can do a 24-month term with co-terming to calendar years, a phased ramp (milestone-based top-ups), an early-credit tranche for Q1, and a short-duration cutover burst lane with usage-based overage pricing and a canary fallback. Below is a concise outline and I'll attach a one-page checklist and draft SOW.

Outline (high level):
- Term: 24 months (2027-01-01 through 2028-12-31) with co-term alignment to calendar years. Early termination options preserved (standard exit clauses).
- Ramp schedule: three tranche schedule — Base Commit (effective 1/1/27), Q1 Top-up (automated credit applied on 2/15/27 after milestone: launch validated), Q2 Permanent uplift (convert top-up to committed capacity on 5/1/27). Each tranche tied to objective metrics (latency, error rate, traffic delta).
- Front-loaded credits: we can provide a limited upfront credit to cover Q1 ramp (one-time credit applied to invoice).
- Cutover/surge band: 30-day post-launch burst pool available for validated cutover (10–20% above commit) with a temporary overage rate that steps down if utilization remains stable. Automatic fallback to a smaller model variant if SLOs degrade.
- Auto-renew: default auto-renew on anniversary, with a 90-day finance opt-out window and a 30-day notice to exercise.

Next steps I recommend:
1) I’ll share the one-pager checklist and a draft SOW for legal/finance to review (attached).
2) If the structure looks good, Camila can open a formal quote and we can model the committed vs burst economics.
3) Karthik to confirm the cutover capacity sizing and the validation metrics.

Attachments: 2026-09-22_StrataMetrics_Rollforward_Summary.xlsx, Redwood_SOW_v2.pdf

Happy to jump on a call — are you free Fri 9/24 or Mon 9/27?

Best,
